Just a story time here, skip if you don’t wanna hear it, has to do with someone who has F U money.
So recently my dad contracted a house. They also hired an interior decorator and usually I don’t like dealing with them but this lady was legit she knew and had been around you could tell. So we frame it up, and as always my dad says talks to the home owner about what’s on the plans, and we never skip the essentials but he will always go over things where we know we could save them money. So the beams they wanted that were on the plans were 25k total for inside and outside big 12x12 beams, we inquired from the salesman that we could get the beams at 13k if we used a different material, I can’t remember the name, we’ve used it on other houses never had any issues and homeowners were happy and it didn’t look any different once it’s stained or finished properly. So homeowner (actually it was rebuilding over the old foundation where his moms burnt down, so his moms house) comes out and my dad goes over A-Z with him and let him know he could save him, no shiat, 120k if we used different materials here and there, but the owner said no just use what’s on the plans (he bought them online from an engineer). So the builder being my dad, and my dad being who he is, every time something came up he would call the owner and say hey we could save you some money here if we did this, and again he would say no just use what’s on the plans. So again we used what’s on the plans. There’s many other things but I’m gonna skip to the end- my dad came under the estimate by 15-20k. I can remember so vividly the look of bewilderment on my dads face when we were all out there standing around the truck of a finished house and the owner said “I was hoping it would come in a little less money then that, but I guess it is what it is”…. My dad is very bi polar (I don’t know if you got a dad like this) and with me and family he’s up and down but to everyone else like the home owners he’s always so nice and he can be a smart azz but the look on his face 😂 I still remember it, the owner started walking towards the house as my dad stood there with this look (I can’t explain it, the complexity in the eyes idk 😂) and then just got in his truck and left. comments.text:
These clips are kinda sensationalist, to be honest.

Yes, this kinda if BS does go on. But it's not every new home being built. 

A lot of it has to do with whether the homes are being built by big corporations that are constantly rushing things and cutting corners and costs.   Or if the home is built by skilled workers that care about doing a good job.

I work in construction for years, and the crews I worked with did good work.

Don't get me wrong, there are some real hacks out there, doing shoddy work. So you have to be diligent.

But these clips can kinda skew your perception, and make you think EVERY new home is poorly made. Which isn't the case.

But you've definitely got to do your home work. If you don't know, then ask who built the home you are looking at. Look into the reputation of the builder.  And always have an independent inspection done, BEFORE you buy.

If a builder tells you that you're not allowed to have your own inspection done, WALK AWAY. That's a HUGE red flag.

comments.text:
You haven't even imagined the crazy stuff that happens on even a remodel of a old house.

I'm Working for a construction company and we were jacking up a 2 story farmhouse to remove the foundation for a new basement.Being added to this house..

This is not just for esthetics, or for the family. Wanted a basement room, this is to save this house. What happened was the previous company that jacked up the house and put a new foundation in under the house.  Decided , instead of rebar inside the foundation , the company decided to install beer cans.. inside the foundation, we arrived construction cleanup. Here is the Foreman showing us around, and he wanted us to help dismantle this foundation, we're getting paid  Eight hours to help do this , and we still get paid eight hours , even if we only take an hour to take it apart , it doesn't even take an hour , that's how bad it was. I walk into the pit with nothing but a baseball bat. That's already a bad sign. When I can walk in with a baseball bat, a metal baseball bat and hit the bottom of the foundation and literally knock out 12 beer cans and weaken the entire structure.

So we're continually hitting the foundation walls, taking them out piece by piece. The house is jacked up above our heads. It's perfectly safe. We've done this, you know, multiple times and within 30 minutes.  We had the entire foundation down and in pieces, and in several pieces, we could just push the foundation over and into the million pieces and shovel everything out.It was a joke holding this house together.

And that isn't even the craziest stuff. I have seen on a job site for a housing development. The most horrific scene I have ever seen in my life that will haunt me for the rest of my life is watching someone fry on a electric panel and trust me, you never want to see it ever.  It will haunt you till the end of your days.

And if you're wondering how it happened, the electrical company failed to check something very important.The building we were working on was next to another building.The two buildings shared a alleyway and underground, which we didn't know about which the electric company had no idea about was a electrical cable that ran from the one building to the other buildings electrical panel.  What we thought was a dead panel after they disconnected, the power was not dead at all. It was still alive when they shut off the power and the electrician had no idea.  And Pretty much cooked on the panel because that underground wire was a jumper, somebody physically jumped a connection from one building's box to another building's box and didn't let any single person know. So, even if you had the main breaker turned off, and the breakers removed and the  Meter outside of the building, disconnected, and the power disconnected that box was still live.Because of a underground electrical cable that no one had a clue was there.

comments.author: @InquisitiveHumanOfficial
comments.text: Something not talked about enough in this arena is the quality of lumber compared to a century or longer ago. The wood used to build structures a century ago was dense, hard, heavy, durable wood. It came from trees that naturally grew without aid over many years, and when harvested the wood was capable of lasting more than a century. We see these old houses all the time, still standing. Lumber nowadays is different. It’s less dense, due to aided growth often on managed tree farms and as a result has less strength and durability. One cannot “make a tree grow faster and bigger and end up with the same as one which grows over time and naturally. Same thing with body building..
